interface.title: Thematic analysis workbench: AI planning-agent pilot (exit interviews)
interface.field: Qualitative research (interview studies, reflexive thematic analysis), applied here to HCI and AI-tool use
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis: reviewing the coding, refining the codebook, checking coverage, building themes and choosing quotes for the write-up
interface.what_it_is_for: A browser workbench where a researcher reviews and corrects an AI agent's coding of interview transcripts. The researcher decides on candidate codes and the agent's proposals, checks coverage per participant, builds themes, and picks verbatim quotes for the paper.

data.note: A prepared analysis folder at /work/app/study/analysis. It holds three exit-interview transcripts: T-01/P1 (4 extracts) and T-02/P2 (3 extracts), both coded, and T-03/P3, left uncoded on purpose. There are 4 codes (control, control.rerun, and two candidates: quality.shallow-codebook and trust.verification), two themes (TH1 accepted with one tension, TH2 a candidate with an open 'asked for claims' request), one pending agent proposal (merge quality.shallow-codebook into trust.verification), an agent comment thread on T-03, RQ1/RQ2, a roster, memos and a v1 changelog. My gestures changed the data: I edited codes, kinds, a span, accepted both candidates, rejected the merge, asked for a re-read, wrote a theme story and selected quotes.

features.name: Coded-transcript reader with extract inspector
features.general: Read a document with its coded spans highlighted. Click or key through each span to open a side pane where you can correct its category, its labels, its notes and its exact boundary.
features.specific: In the Transcript view, coloured spans and extract chips sit under each turn. j/k walk them, and 1/2/3 set said/did/intent. The pane offers '+ code' with a searchable picker that previews definitions, × to remove a code, context and note fields, 'adjust the boundary', '★ flag this quote' and 'drop this extract'. Context and flag edits are applied at once with an 'Applied' toast; kind and code edits show as '1 staged' in the pane.
steps: click a span or chip, or press j/k
read the code definitions with include/exclude in the pane
press 1/2/3 or the kind buttons to fix said/did/intent
add a code with '+ code' or remove one with ×
type context or a note
press 'Done with T-xx' to mark the rest reviewed
serves_tasks: Read each coded passage beside the code definition it is meant to meet
Correct which codes a passage carries
Record the circumstances of a passage and mark it as worth quoting
Change whether a passage is something said, done or intended
Sign off an interview as reviewed

features.name: Transcript filter bar
features.general: Narrow a coded document to one kind of evidence, one category or the passages flagged as quotable, so only those spans stay highlighted
features.specific: Transcript toolbar: ● said / ▶ did / ◇ intent counters that toggle each kind, an 'all codes' list to pick one code, and '★ only'. 'new only' sits beside them but was not tried.
steps: press a said/did/intent counter to hide that kind
choose a code in the 'all codes' list
toggle '★ only' to keep flagged extracts
toggle the filters off to reset
serves_tasks: Narrow the transcript to certain kinds of evidence or codes

features.name: Re-trim a span by selecting text
features.general: Change the exact start and end of a quoted passage by selecting the words in the source, so the stored text is always cut from the original and never retyped
features.specific: Press 'adjust the boundary'. A bar asks you to select the words to keep inside the extract's own turn; select them and press 're-trim E-xxxx to the selection'. The Quotes view's 'trim for inline use' → select in the side pane's copy of the quote → 'trim it' does the same for a shortened inline quote.
steps: press 'adjust the boundary' (or 'trim for inline use')
drag-select the words to keep (for inline trims, in the side pane's copy)
press 're-trim … to the selection' (or 'trim it')
see the toast or the 'TRIM IN FLIGHT' tag
serves_tasks: Tighten the boundary of a coded passage without retyping it
Shorten a quote for use in a sentence without altering the words

features.name: Code co-occurrence matrix with pair compare
features.general: A heatmap of how often two categories label the same item, switchable between raw count and Jaccard. Hover for the figures, and click a cell to see the two categories side by side with what each holds alone and together, plus merge actions.
features.specific: Codebook → overlap: switch shared count/jaccard. Parent–child cells are greyed out. Hovering gives a tooltip; clicking opens 'control vs control.rerun' with only/both columns, '→ control.rerun' moves and 'merge A → B' buttons. 'Pairs worth a decision' and 'Codes carrying the most' list the suspects (both empty in this data).
steps: press overlap
choose shared count or jaccard
hover a cell to read the figures
click the cell to compare the pair
move single extracts or merge (not tried), or close
serves_tasks: Find codes that overlap and compare a pair side by side

features.name: Codebook tree with per-code decision pane
features.general: A hierarchical list of categories showing prevalence bars and health flags. Picking one shows all its evidence by participant, its editable definition, the proposer's rationale, and accept/retire/split/rename/fold actions.
features.specific: In the Codebook structure view: health chips at the top (≤1 participant, candidate, never reviewed…), tree rows with an n/N bar and kind glyphs, and a pane with name/definition/include/exclude ✎, 'The agent's case for this code', 'accept into the codebook' / 'back to candidate' / retire / split a child out / rename, fold-into or make-child-of, and 'place here too' in a theme. Only accept was used.
steps: pick a code in the tree
read its extracts grouped by participant
read the agent's case and its borderline extract
press accept into the codebook
check the candidate count drop and the header's 'unapplied → v2' tally
serves_tasks: Read one code across all participants to check it was applied consistently
Decide which proposed codes join the scheme

features.name: Coverage matrix with re-read request
features.general: A category × participant count grid with n/N and the said/did/intent split. Click a filled cell to read its evidence, or an empty cell to send a 'look again' request for that source.
features.specific: Coverage: a P3 'no extracts' banner, a matrix with collapsible code families, and tables of transcripts and participants (with 'families never applied to them' chips). An empty cell opens 'Ask for a re-read' with a 'what to look for' box. Once sent, the cell shows ⟲.
steps: read n/N and said/did/intent per code
click a filled cell to list its extracts
click an empty cell or family chip
type what to look for
press 'ask for a re-read of T-03' and see ⟲ in the cell
serves_tasks: See what lies behind each prevalence count
Ask for a participant with no coding to be read again

features.name: Proposal inbox (accept / reject / resolve)
features.general: A drawer of changes and comments the assistant has staged. Accept carries a change out now, reject drops it, and threads are resolved separately.
features.specific: 'Pending (n)' opens 'Waiting for the agent'. It lists 'Proposed by the agent' entries such as op-0001 merge, with a rationale and accept/reject (plus 'accept all') and the ta.py apply command, and 'Threads' such as op-0002 and op-0008 with ✓ resolve. Clicking a thread jumps to the view it belongs to.
steps: press Pending
read a proposal's rationale
press accept or reject
see the count drop and the staged marker leave the code tree
resolve threads (not tried)
serves_tasks: Resolve the assistant's pending suggestions

features.name: Theme card editor (brief, story, tensions, paper status)
features.general: A side pane for one theme: write its claim, summary, scope note and story; tie it to a research question; mark which pieces of evidence complicate it; set its importance for the paper; ask the assistant for candidate codes or claims
features.specific: Click a theme header on the board to edit name/essence/brief/story with ✎ (save, or '💬 ask instead'). The pane also has the RQ dropdown, in the paper undecided/headline/secondary/no, 'ask for candidate codes' / 'ask for claims', fold into or drop this theme, tensions with remove, extracts by participant each with a 'tension' button, and '💬 ask about this theme'. The RQ dropdown, 'ask for claims', fold/drop and '💬 ask about this theme' were not used.
steps: click the theme header
press ✎ on story, type and save
press tension on a complicating extract
set in the paper to headline
press ask for candidate codes
serves_tasks: Read a theme's claim, summary, scope note and the evidence under it
Write in a few sentences what a theme says
Mark the evidence that complicates a theme
Decide how prominently a theme figures in the paper
Ask the assistant to propose codes for a theme

features.name: Theme board
features.general: A board with one column per theme, plus columns for miscellaneous and not-yet-placed categories, each showing its category cards and its status for the paper; a theme's header opens its editor
features.specific: Themes view: columns TH1, TH2, miscellaneous and unplaced with code cards; the TH2 card shows 'headline' once set. Clicking a header opens the theme card editor (f7); pressing a code card opens that code in Codebook. Dragging a card to another column timed out twice and the 'place here too' dropdown did not apply, so moving codes between themes is unconfirmed.
steps: open Themes and read the columns
check each theme's paper status on its card
click a theme header to open its editor
click a code card to open it in Codebook
serves_tasks: Read a theme's claim, summary, scope note and the evidence under it
Decide how prominently a theme figures in the paper

features.name: Quote bank and selection with attribution spread
features.general: Filter the pool of candidate quotes for a theme, move chosen ones into a list for the paper, and watch a per-participant spread table and warnings about over-reliance or missing behavioural evidence
features.specific: Quotes: filters for theme, participant, code, said·did·intent, order and ★ only. 'The bank' has 'use in the paper', 'trim for inline use' and 'mark as the tension'. 'In the paper' has ↑/↓, trim and remove; ↑ took two clicks and the order reverted moments later, so reordering does not persist. The 'Attribution spread' table and the '⚠ TH2 has 1 did extract but no did quote selected' warning update as you choose.
steps: choose the theme
press use in the paper on chosen extracts
check the attribution spread and that the warnings have cleared
trim one for inline use
serves_tasks: Choose quotes for a theme and keep the evidence balanced
Shorten a quote for use in a sentence without altering the words

features.name: Comment thread on an item
features.general: Attach a question to a specific coded passage, code or theme for the assistant to answer, without changing the data
features.specific: '💬 ask about this coding / code / theme' opens 'What is the doubt?'. 'Leave the thread' stages op-xxxx, the thread appears on the card and in Pending → Threads, and the header count rises to '2 threads'.
steps: press 💬 ask about this coding
type the doubt
press Leave the thread
see the thread on the card and in Pending
serves_tasks: Raise a doubt about a coding decision for the agent to answer

features.name: Header status line
features.general: A running tally of the analysis state: codebook version and how many decided changes are not yet applied, open comment threads, and how many proposals are waiting
features.specific: Header: codebook version with 'n unapplied → v2' (rose from 2 to 3 as candidates were accepted), 'n threads' (1 → 2 after a new thread), and 'Pending (n)', which opens the proposal inbox (f6).
steps: read the unapplied → v2 tally after a codebook decision
read the thread count after leaving a doubt
press Pending (n) to open the inbox
serves_tasks: Decide which proposed codes join the scheme
Resolve the assistant's pending suggestions

screens_never_reached: An open view of the agent's thread op-0002 (comment on T-03) with a reply box: clicking it in Pending jumped to Coverage, and neither Coverage nor the T-03 transcript pane showed the thread (screens/022.webp, screens/023.webp, screens/045.webp)
The agent's proposed codes and claims shown as dashed cards on TH2: these appear only after the agent runs its next pass, which this browser cannot trigger
The mermaid export of the theme board, '+ theme', and the Codebook 'Done with this round' result: not tried within the action budget
Video frames beside transcripts: 'no frames beside this transcript' for every interview
not_done: Replying to the comment thread: no reply box could be reached for op-0002, and only '✓ resolve' was offered in Pending, so the thread was neither answered nor resolved

Grouping codes into themes: dragging codes on the Themes board and in the Codebook tree timed out after 45 s both times, and the press registered as a click that opened the code in Codebook (screens/048.webp, screens/052.webp). Creating a theme, moving a code between themes and putting a code in a second theme therefore stayed unseen. The 'place here too' dropdown fallback did not apply via keyboard (screens/054.webp).
Reordering quotes in 'In the paper': ↑ on E-0004 (screens/057.webp) seemed to move it, but the replay found the first click did nothing and a second click's move reverted moments later
Accepting an agent proposal: the only one (op-0001) was rejected on purpose because the agent's own case argued the two codes are distinct; 'accept all' was not tried
Judging the agent's proposals for a theme: 'ask for candidate codes' was sent for TH2, but the proposed codes and claims arrive only on the agent's next pass, so none could be accepted or rejected

The frozen-codebook recoding pass and applying staged changes: these run through ta.py on the command line ('apply --all'), outside the browser; reviewing what that pass added with 'new only' was therefore not done
Handing the round back to the agent: no hand-back step was tried or seen in the browser, so where a review round ends is not recorded
